abstract: By the grand canonical Monte Carlo method,physisorption of hydrogen storage in single-walled boron nitride nanotube arrays(SWBNNTA) at moderate pressure with normal temperature is studied.The influences of tube diameter,distance between tubes and pressure on hydrogen physisorption in SWBNNTA are investigated.It indicates that at normal temperature and moderate pressure the hydrogen storage capacity(mass percent) of SWBNNTA is obviously greater than that of single-walled carbon nanotube arrays,and exceeds the commercial standard presented by U.S.Department of Energy.Corresponding theoretical explanation is given.

title: Progress of Study on Single Walled Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: Single wall carbon nanotubes(SWCNTs) is an advanced nanomaterial,the mainly preparation methods includes arc_discharge method,chemical vapor deposition(catalytic pyrolysis) and laser_vaporization,while CVD is an efficient synthesis methods of SWCNTs.For its characteristics,such as high strength while low density,unique optical,electromagnetic and thermal properties,and hydrogen-storage property,carbon nanotube can be extensively applied in aviation,aerospace,military and medicine industries.

title: Hydrogen Absorption and Desorption Properties of MgH_2-graphene Compound Hydrogen Storage Materials
venue: Journal of Anhui University of Technology
abstract: MgH2,MgH2-G and MgH2-graphene hydrogen storage materials were prepared by ball milling.The effect of addition of graphene on the hydrogen absorption and desorption properties of MgH2 was investigated.It was found that the additions of graphite and grapheme can promote the fine of MgH2.The hydrogen absorption and desorption properties of MgH2-G and MgH2-graphene compounds were improved after the addition of graphite and graphene.Especially the hydrogen desorption and re-absorption contents of the MgH2-graphene compound are 7.0% at 573 K within 5,2 min,respectively.The hydrogen desorption starting temperature of this compound is lower than that of MgH2 for 50 K.

title: The Possibility of Hydrogen Storage on/in Carbon Nano-tube (CNT) Based on DFTB Analysis
venue: Journal of Guilin University of Electronic Technology
abstract: Carbon nano-tube (CNT) have attracted the attention of the whole world since it was claimed to be the exclusive candidate carrier of hydrogen for the hydrogen vehicle. However,reports on hydrogen uptake of the materials are quite controversial. In this review, based on DFTB(the density-functional based tight-binding method), the interactions between hydrogen atom and microstructure of CNT have been introduced.A further discussion is about the structural and electronic properties of C_(60)-H and CNT-H composite. It is shown that the permeation of molecular hydrogen (H_2) through the carbon network of the C_(60) and CNT is strongly suppressed, and the formation of H-CNT by discharge of hydrogen ions as a possible basic step for an electrochemical-based hydrogen storage in CNT is discussed.

title: Chemical Activation and Hydrogen Storage Properties of Mesoporous Carbon CMK-3
abstract: Activation of mesoporous carbon CMK-3 with KOH,NaOH,H3PO4 was studied.Huge structure and texture changes emerge for the activated CMK-3 based on the characterization by using XRD,low temperature nitrogen adsorption-desorption.The ordered mesoporous structure of CMK-3 gradually became disorder,specic surface area and mesoporous(2 nm)were enhanced remarkably.The effect on activation results was studied of mass ratio for CMK-3 to KOH,activation temperature,chemical used.Hydrogen sorption measurement shows that the activation leads to an obvious increase in the H2 sorption capacity of CMK-3.The H2 uptake of 2.32wt% at 77 K and 100 kPa was obtained.

title: THE SYNTHESIS AND HYDROGEN UPTAKE OF HIGH-PURITY SINGLE-WALLED CARBON NANOTUBES
abstract: Large\|scale synthesis of single\|walled carbon nanotubes(SWNT)is a key issue for both fundamental research and application exploration of this novel material.High\|quality SWNTs were synthesized on a large scale by a hydrogen arc discharge method.Moreover,it was found that,under about 100atm of hydrogen and at room temperature,a hydrogen storage capacity of (4\^2\_4\^7)wt% could be achieved for the suitably pre\|treated SWNTs,and after 5 cyclic measurements,the capacity was at first marginally decreased and then kept stable.These preliminary results indicate that SWNTs may be a very promising candidate for hydrogen storage materials.

title: Preparation and adsorption properties of high density resorcinol-formaldehyde carbonized aerogel ICF target
venue: High Power Laser and Particle Beams
abstract: High density resorcinol-formaldehyde carbonized aerogel(CRF) ICF target was prepared from resorcinol and formaldehyde by improving synthesis conditions,and the cracking problem of high density CRF aerogels was solved.The elements and phase of CRF carbonized aerogels were analyzed.N2 and H2 adsorption properties of the aerogels were analyzed with Autosorb-1.The results show that the CRF carbonized aerogels is a kind of non-crystalline graphite-like solids mainly composed of carbon,the aerogels has homogeneous structure and excellent processable characteristic.The specific surface area and the average pore diameter of the aerogels are 676 m2·g-1 and 7.16 nm,respectively.The aerogel has a favorable hydrogen adsorption with a mass percent of 2.28% and a volumetric density of 17.83 kg·m-3.

title: The effect of carbon nanotubes on the electrochemical hydrogen storage performance of MmNi_5-type alloy
abstract: The electrochemical hydrogen storage performance of MmNi5-type electrodes doped with carbon nanotubes(CNTs) in an alkaline solution was investigated with cyclic voltammetry(CV) and chronopotentiometry(CP). The results showed that the electrochemical hydrogen storage performance of MmNi5-type electrodes doped with CNTs was notably improved. Furthermore, electrochemical activation ability of the electrode with the CNTs and MmNi5 weight ratio of 1∶16.7 was the most excellent, and the discharging capacity increased to 62.41%.

title: Influence of Piezoelectric Element on Hydrogen Adsorption of Pt--supported Activated Carbon
abstract: Mixing Pt-coated activated carbon with secondary activated carbon as adsorbent was used for hydrogen storage.Behaviors of hydrogen adsorption on Pt-supported activated carbon in the presence of a piezoelectric element were investigated.Hydrogen storage in activated carbons can be increased by secondary hydrogen spillover from a supported Pt catalyst.The piezoelectric element is able to autogenously generate charges in hydrogen pressure.The observed adsorption enhancements of NAC,Pt/NAC-1,Pt/NAC-2 and Pt/NAC-3 are 15%,36.5%,39.3%and 43.9%,respectively.The greater enhancement observed from hydrogen adsorption on Pt/NAC samples can be attributed to charges generated by PMN-PT facilitate dissociation of hydrogen molecules into hydrogen atoms.The easier accessibility of the atomic orbital might favor the electron transfer from the atomic hydrogen to charged carbon.

title: HYDROGEN ADSORPTION AND STORAGE IN CARBON NANOTUBES
abstract: Hydrogen adsorption sorage in carbon nanotubes has been arising great interesting the study of nanostructured carbon materials and novel hydrogen energy utilization technologies,because of its special structure and properties.The existing experimental studies and theoretical research on hydrogen storage in carbon nanotubes have shown the good storage capacity and optentic potental application.Futher studies,both extensively theoretical investigation and more sophisticated experimental method shoud be perfomed to achieve a good undestanding of hydrogen adsorption behavior in the carbon nanotubes.

title: A report on the Carbon2003 conference in Oviedo, Spain
abstract: This is a brief report on the Carbon2003 conference held in Oviedo of Spain in the second week of July 2003. More than 400 experts from 38 nations presented 516 contributions of the most recent results of their research on carbon. Similar to previous carbon meetings, a wide range of topica was covered, including Raw Materials and Thermal Treatments, Fibres and Composites, New Carbon Forms, Advanced Structural Characterization, Adsorption and Surface Science, Chemical Reactivity, Intercalation and Catalysis, Energy Storage, Environmental Applications, Other Products/Applications (Biomaterials, etc.). The Carbon2003 conference is especially characterized by introducing a novel debate forum on Hot Topics with the aim of provoking discussion and debate on unresolved questions and highly controversial issues, including magnetic carbon or ferromagnetism in pure carbon, potentiomatric titrations for the characterization of functional groups on carbons, hydrogen storage in SWCNTs, methane storage in microporous carbons and the nature of basic sites on carbon surfaces as well as a novel structure of nongraphitizing carbons, etc. It is believed that this kind of Hot Topic forum should be adopted in all future carbon conferences.

title: Recent Research on Carbon Nanotubes(CNT) and Hydrogen Storage Properties
abstract: The preparation and purification methods of the CNT were summarized and the research of hydrogen storage experiments was emphasized in this study.The direction of hydrogen storage on carbon nanotubes was also suggested.

title: Stability,Electronic and Magnetic Properties of ZnS Nanotubes:A Comparative Study
abstract: Electronic and magnetic properties of ZnS nanotubes(NTs) were investigated systematically using first-principles approach.A double-wall NT(DWNT) with hexagonal cross section(HCS) shows higher stability,while zigzag and armchair NTs with round cross section(RCS) show lower stability than single-wall NT(SWNT) with HCS.Electronic band structures show that they are direct band gap semiconductors.With hydrogen adsorption,SWNT with HCS transform into indirect band gap semiconductor.Magnetic properties of ZnS NTs doped with transition-metal(TM) atoms(Cr,Mn,Fe,Co,and Ni) are calculated.Formation energies of doped NTs are smaller than those of the pristine ones,indicating that doing process is an exothermic reaction.All NTs have atom-like magnetic moments mainly due to 3d component of the TM atoms.Monodoped NTs have potential utility in materials with tunable magnetic properties.

title: Molecular Dynamics Simulate of Hydrogen Physisorption in Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: The process of hydrogen physisorption in single walled carbon nanotubes can be simulated with molecular dynamic method.The relationships between hydrogen storage capacity of SWCNT and temperature,pressure,SWCNT's diameter are studied systemically,the adsorption isotherms in carbon nanotubes of typical diameter can be worked out,which can be used in Grand canonical ensemble.

title: RESEARCH ON PREPARATION OF CARBON NANO-SPHERE
abstract: Using apo-ferritin as raw material,a new carbon nano-sized material,hollow carbon nano-sphere,has been prepared with biological template method in this paper.Compared to carbon nanotube,hollow carbon nano-sphere has special microstructure,small proportion(1.3 mg/m3),larger specific surface area( 600 m2/g),and abundant nano-sized void.Therefore,it has remarkably potential application in hydrogen storage material and anode material for lithium secondary batteries.

title: Performance of hydrogen storage of carbon nanotubes decorated with palladium
abstract: Carbon nanotubes(CNTs) decorated with palladium were synthesized and applied to hydrogen storage of gas phase. The results show that the amount of hydrogen storage of the decorated CNTs is up to 3.9%(mass fraction), of which, almost 85% H_2 can be desorbed at ambient temperature and pressure, while the non-decorated CNTs has a poor performance of hydrogen storage(only about 0.5%H_2, mass fraction). These indicate that it is feasible to enhance the performance of hydrogen storage of CNTs by further decoration with hydrogen-storing metals or alloys.

title: Modification of Multi-walled Carbon Nanotubes and Its Performance for Hydrogen Storage
Progress of Research on Hydrogen Storage Materials
abstract: Hydrogen as one new power sources has attracted great attentions recently all over the world. The technologies of hydrogen storage and transport is a key problems for hydrogen application and are developing constantly now. In present paper, recent research developments on hydrogen storage materials including hydrogen storage alloys carbon nanotube, graphite nanofigre, Ti-doped alkali metal-aluminium hydrides and some liquid organic hydrides are reviewed. In addition some prepareation methods developed recently for hydrogen materials are also introduced.

title: Hydrogen storage properties of Mg-based materials with CNTs
venue: The Chinese Journal of Nonferrous Metals
abstract: Nanocomposite Mg-3Ni-2MnO-0.25CNTs was made by mechanical ball milling method under hydrogen pressure of 0.5MPa. The nanocomposite has very high Absorption hydrogen capacity and remarkable kinetic properties in hydriding /dehydriding process, for example the nanocomposite can Absorb 7.0% hydrogen in 100s at 200℃ under of hydrogen pressure of 2.0MPa. The grain of Mg-based hydrogen storage materials with CNTs is much smaller in ball milling process than that of the materials without CNTs. The composites has potential application in the future.

title: Preparation of graphene with high hydrogen storage properties by the high-vacuum and low-temperature chemical exfoliation method
abstract: Graphite oxide(GO) was prepared by hummers liquid oxidation method and the graphene with high surface area was then prepared by a high-vacuum and low-temperature chemical exfoliation method.The as-prepared GNS was characterized by X-ray diffraction(XRD),Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy(FT-IR),X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy(XPS),Raman spectra(RS),scanning electron microscopy(SEM) and transmission electron microscopy(TEM),respectively.The results indicate that graphite oxide is completely reduced to graphene and the graphene possesses a plicated layer structure with few defects.BET measurement and hydrogen adsorption experiment results show that the BET specific surface area of the graphene was about 908.3m2/g with rich pore structure and that hydrogen storage capacity of H2 on graphene reached up to 1.81%,0.995% and 0.44wt% at 25,40,55℃ respectively,GNS was one of promising materials in the field of hydrogen storage.

title: Simulation of Hydrogen Transport in a Single-walled Carbon Nanotube for Storage Safety
abstract: Carbon nanotubes hold much promise as future materials for safe storage of hydrogen. In this paper, hydrogen transport mechanisms in single-walled carbon nano-tubes (SWNTs) for various temperatures and chiral indices were studied using molecular dynamics simulation method. The SWNT models of zigzag (10,0), chiral (10,5) and armchair (10,10) with hydrogen molecules inside were simulated at temperatures ranging from 253K to 373K. Movements of hydrogen molecules () inside a SWNT were analyzed using mean-square displacements and velocity autocorrelation functions.

title: Ball Milling Process and Its Effect on Hydrogen Adsorption Storage of MWNTS
abstract: The effect of mechanical ball milling with different time on the hydrogen adsorption behavior of the multi-wall carbon nanotubes(MWNTs)was studied.The microstructure characteristics of MWNTs before and after ball milling were examined by transmission electron microscope(TEM)and X-ray diffraction(XRD).The results showed that ball milling could break MWNTs,shorten their length,open the tips of the tubes,and increased their surface defects and specific surface area at the same time.After ball milling for 12 h,the hydrogen storage capacity of MWNTs increased from 1.60% to 2.55%.The enhancement of hydrogen adsorption might result from the increase of defects and surface area of the MWNTs caused by ball milling.

title: HYDROGEN STORAGE OF MINERALS
abstract: In this paper, the concept of hydrogen storage of minerals was proposed. The minerals having hydrogen storage performance should have structural nano-ecaled channels or pores, and the channels or pores may be distributed on one dimension or multi-dimension in space. The experimental research progresses of hydrogen storage of minerals including crystal graphite, zeolite and palygorskite-sepiolite group etc. were reviewed, at the same time, the mechanism of hydrogen storage of minerals was discussed. At last, the research trends of hydrogen storage of minerals were suggested.

title: Adsorption on Two-dimensional Boron and Carbon Based Nanostructures and Properties
abstract: We review physical properties and potential applications of two-dimensional boron and carbon based nanostructures such as graphene and BC3sheet adsorbed with metal atoms,non-metal atoms or molecules. Pristine graphene is semi-metallic with zero band gap,which is nonmagnetic and has weak spin orbit coupling( SOC). BC3sheet is a semiconductor with an indirect band gap. As graphene and BC3sheet are adsorbed with metal atoms,non-metal atoms or molecules,graphene systems may have a band gap at Dirac point,strong SOC,magnetic order and superconductivity. Applications in hydrogen storage may be realized in graphene and BC3systems. In addition,it has been demonstrated that graphene can be used as gas sensors with significantly high precision.

title: Progress of Research on Uniform Dispersion and Application of Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: The structure and properties of carbon nanotubes and dispersion methods for them were introduced,and the progress of research on their application in several important areas,such as electronic devices,electrode materials,hydrogen storage materials,composites and catalyst were described.In addition,the application prospect of carbon nanotubes in leather industry was proposed.

title: Comparative Study About the Physical & Chemical and Catal Ytic Perfomance of Various Ni-B Amorphous Alloy Catalysts
abstract: Ni-B amorphous alloy catalysts supported on Al_2O_3、SiO_2、CNTs were prepared by impregnation-chemical reduction method and Ni-B amorphous alloy prepared by chemical reduction method.Catalysts were characterized by transmission electron microscopy(TEM),inductively coupled plasma(ICP),X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy(XPS),temperature programmed desorption of hydrogen(H_2-TPD) as well as CO-chemisorption,and studied in the selective hydrogenation of acetylene.Results of experiment showed that introduction of Al_2O_3、SiO_2、CNTs supports to Ni-B amorphous alloy catalysts promoted the dispersion of Ni-B particles and increased the surface area of active nickel differently.Mean size of 10nm Ni-B particles were dispersed along the nanotubes homogeneously,leading to 30.6 m~2/g surface area of active nickel and the best amount of hydrogen adsorption,which shows the perfect performance of Ni-B/CNTs among all catalysts.In addition,electrons transferred partially from nanotubes to nickel in the Ni-B amorphous alloy,making electron-rich nickel.As a result,Ni-B/CNTs catalyst exhibited better acetylene hydrogenation activity than other catalysts;Ni-B catalyst exhibited the lowest ethylene selectivity.

title: Potential applications of carbon nanotubes in battery industry
abstract: The structure of carbon nanotubes was introduced briefly. The potential applications of carbon nanotubes were described. Carbon nanotubes were prospective hydrogen-storage material, which could absorb/adsorb a large quantity of hydrogen and did the reversible adsorption/absorption process repeatedly .As electrode material for Li-ion battery , carbon nanotubes had a higher lithium capacity than graphite and performed good cycle performance. The catalyst of fuel cell , prepared by depositing noble metal on carbon nanotubes ,could decrease the mass of noble metal, reduce the size of catalyst and improve the catalyst performance.

title: Molecular dynamics simulation of hydrogen physisorption in single-walled carbon nanotube arrays
abstract: Processes of hydrogen physisorption in single-walled carbon nanotube arrays(SWCNTA) with different tube diameters and inter-tube distances are simulated by the molecular dynamics method on the condition of different pressure at normal temperature.The influences of pressure,tube diameter and inter-tube distance on hydrogen physisorption in SWCNTA,inside of the tubes and in the tube interstices,have been investigated in detail.We find that hydrogen molecules are mostly absorbed near the tube walls of SWCNTA,and increasing the tube diameter and inter-tube distance properly can improve the hydrogen storage capacity of SWCNTA effectively,which makes SWCNTA have higher capability for hydrogen storage at normal temperature.And their theoretic explanations are also given.Our computational results show that the total gravimetric hydrogen storage capacity of SWCNTA can reach 4.2% at normal temperature and moderate pressure,and offer a theoretical support for the experimental results,which reported in Ref. that the gravimetric hydrogen storage capacity of SWCNTA at normal temperature and moderate pressure is 4.2%.

title: SYNTHESIS AND APPLICATIONS OF GRAPHENE
abstract: This paper summarized the extraordinarily physical and electrical properties of graphene,including electron transport-Massless Dirac Fermion behav ior,Anomalous quantum Hall effect(chiral,RT) ,Minimum quantum conductivity,Suppression of quantum interference effect,and etc.The mechanical and chemical synthesis methods for graphene and the applications of graphene in nanoelectronic devices,computer chip replace of silicon,manufacturing the fastest transistor,reducing yawp and potential hydrogen storage,etc were also introduced.

title: Development of Helical Carbon Nanofibers
abstract: Helical carbon nanofibers have been attracting tremendous attention due to their novel physical and chemical properties(low-desity,super-elasticity,high electric conductivity,high specific strength,heat resistance and chemical stability).They can be used as micro-magnetic sensors,electromagnetic wave absorption materials,hydrogen storage materials and elastic materials,etc.The preparation,influence factors,microstructure,and growth mechanism of helical carbon nanofibers are reviewed.Some problems in the research of helical carbon nanofibers are also summarized.

title: The Preparation of Super Activated Carbons and its properties for Hydrogen Storage
abstract: A series of super activated carbons were prepared by high sulfur pertroleum cokes.The properties of super activated carbon for H 2 storage were studied systemically in the range of 93～293K at 20K intervas and pressure up to 10MPa.The results showed that hydrogen storage capacities increased with the surface area of super activated carbon.The amounts of adsorbed hydrogen by weight were respectively 1 9wt%、9 8wt% in the condition of 293K/5MP工93K/6 0MPa and the ratio of desorption was 95 9% for the super activated carbon with the BET surface area of 3886m 2/g.

title: The Electrochemical Hydrogen Storage Properties of Ordered Mesoporous Carbons
abstract: Ordered mesoporous carbon materials were successfully synthesized by an easy method of the carbonization of sulfuric-acid-treated silica/triblock copolymer/sucrose composites.The morphologies,structures and pore characteristics of the carbon materials were investigated by X-ray diffraction(XRD),nitrogen adsorption desorption and transmission electron microscopy(TEM and HRTEM)measurements.On the basis of comparing the surface areas and pore properties of two ordered mesoporous carbons obtained by changing the content of the reactants,their electrochemical hydrogen storage capacities were tested by Galvanostatic charge-discharge measurement.The results showed that the carbon material(C-P)with higher specific surface area(720m~2·g~(-1))and pore volume(0.86cm~3·g~(-1))had higher hydrogen storage capacity(70.1mAh·g~(-1))than the carbon material(C-S)(64.1mAh·g~(-1))with lower specific surface area(610m~2·g~(-1))and pore volume(0.66cm~3·g~(-1)).Both of the two ordered mesoporous carbons exhibited higher hydrogen storage capacities than the single-walled carbon nanotubes(25.9mAh·g~(-1)).The cyclic voltammetry measurement indicated that the ordered mesoporous carbon electrode possessed higher electrochemical activity than single-walled carbon nanotubes electrode.

title: Progress of research on hydrogen storage materials
venue: Journal of Shandong Institute of Light Industry
abstract: Hydrogen as a clean and green resource of energy has attracted extensive attention on hydrogen research and application all over the world.The use of hydrogen energy is benefical to the environmental protection,the reduction of pollution,and the effective use of energy.The sorts of hydrogen storage materials and its recent research development are summarized in this paper,and its properties are introduced simplely.The mentioned hydrogen storage materials in this paper include alloy hydrogen storage materials,light metal-aluminum hydride,glass microsphere,carbon nanotubes,activated carbon with high specific surface area,organic liquid hydride.

title: Adsorption equilibrium of hydrogen on activated carbon YK-1
abstract: The adsorption equilibrium of hydrogen on the coconut shell activated carbon YK-1 was analyzed based on the adsorption data volumetrically measured over a temperature-pressure range respectively within 113-293 K and 0-12.5 MPa.Isosteric heats of hydrogen adsorption at four adsorption amounts and limit values under zero surface coverage were determined by adsorption isosteres and the Henry plot of the adsorption data within 10% surface coverage,respectively.A lattice theory based Ono-Kondo model was applied for model study of the adsorption data,linear regression of the equation was carried out to determine the maximum adsorption capacity,the adsorption potential and the correlating parameter.The results show that the isosteric heat of adsorption varies evenly with the adsorption amount,the mean and limit values are respectively 4.64 kJ/mol and 5.37 kJ/mol;the model can much accurately predict the isotherms,and the maximum adsorption capacity decreases with temperature with its value smaller than that of the liquid hydrogen.The adsorptive performance of hydrogen can be enhanced on an activated carbon by increasing its specific surface area and the micropore volume as well as properly lowering down the temperature of the storage system.

title: FABRICATION AND PERFORMANCE OF A MINI POWER SOURCE WITH A PLANAR SIX-CELL PEM UNITIZED REGENERATIVE FUEL CELL STACK
venue: Journal of South China Normal University
abstract: A novel micro planar fuel cell power supplier,in which a six-cell PEM united regenerative fuel cell(URFC) stack is used as the power generator,was designed and fabricated.Each cell was made by sandwiching a membrane electrode assembly(MEA) between two graphite monopolar plates,and six cell units were mechanically fixed in two organic glass endplates.When the stack was operated in electrolysis mode,hydrogen was generated from the splitting of water and stored in hydrogen storage alloy;when it was operated in fuel cell mode,hydrogen was supplied by the hydrogen storage alloy and oxygen was supplied from air.At room temperature and atmospheric pressure,the open-circuit voltage of the system reached 4.9 V,the system could be discharged at a constant current density of 19 mA/cm2 for about 40 min,and the work voltage was 3.0 V.The system showed good stability for 10 charge-discharge cycles.

title: Recent progress about graphene for chemical energy storage applications
abstract: The unique two-dimensional spatial structure gives graphene excellent chemical and physical properties and huge specific surface area. These make graphene a very promising material for energy storage applications. This paper reviews recent progress in the use of graphene in chemical energy storage, including hydrogen storage, supercapacitor, lithium ion batteries, lithium-sulfur batteries and lithium-air batteries. Relationships between different preparation methods of graphene and their chemical/electrochemical properties are discussed. Graphene could form three dimensional conductive network to enhance the electrochemical properties of electrodes materials, but also provide a buffer for the volume change during charging-discharging processes to extend the life-span. Further improvements of electrochemical performance are able to be achieved by optimizing the microstructure of composite materials. Finally, key issues related to practical applications of graphene are briefly discussed.

title: Development of Hydrogen Storage Tanks for Fixed Fuel Cells
abstract: Based on the application of hydrogen storage tanks for fixed fuel cells,the carbon fiber wrapped hydrogen storage tanks with 12 L were developed.The tensile strength of CYD-128 resin casting was analyzed,and the NOL ring interfacial shear strength of T700/CYD-128 was also researched.Furthermore,the fiber layer design was implemented by the utilizing of CADWIND,which was testified by finite element analysis.The results of explosion test and pressure cycle test showed that the designed hydrogen storage tank reached the desired requirements.

title: Research on influence factors and preparation of carbon nanometer ball hydrogen storage material
abstract: With the anthracite coal de-ashed,carbonized,pre-graphited and mixed with activated metals,the carbon nanometer ball hydrogen storage materials could be made with the reaction ball grinding method in hydrogen atmosphere.The paper studied the raw material pretreatment,hydrogen pressurization,activated metal and others influenced to the performances of the hydrogen storage material.During the high energy reaction ball grinding,the material could reach to 30~50 nm in a short time.Then the material would have a high hydrogen storage density and a low hydrogen releasing temperature.During the hydrogen storage period,the magnesium and carbon would have coordinative effect.The Al,Co,Fe and Ni metal catalysts could obviously improve the hydriding and dehydriding performaces of the hydrogen storage material and could promote the coordinative affect between Mg and C.

title: PRELIMINARY STUDY ON HYDROGEN STORAGE IN CARBON NANOFIBERS
abstract: We present the results of hydrogen storage in carbon nanofibers (CNF) synthesized using the thermal decomposition of selected hydrocarbons over Fe Cu metal catalyst particles. The maximum capacity of hydrogen adsorption is 9.99 wt% which is six times higher than that in usual LaNi 5. It is also found that CNF can rapidly release hydrogen at room temperature. However, mechanizm of this phenomenon has not yet been understood.

title: ADSORPTION OF HYDROGEN IN DIFFERENT STRUCTURAL SINGLE-WALLED CARBON NANOTUBE ARRAYS
venue: Journal of Chemical Industry and Engineering
abstract: The adsorption of hydrogen in square and triangular single walled carbon nanotube arrays was studied with grand canonical ensemble Monte Carlo method The adsorption isotherm was simulated at 77 K , 133 K and 298 K, and the ability of hydrogen adsorption storage in two different structural SWNTA was compared The reason for the difference in adsorption ability of the two SWNTA was analyzed according to potential field distribution, and the potential field distribution of different tube diameters and different inter tube spacings and the effect of potential field distribution on adsorption ability were discussed.The inter tube spacing is the key factor inducing the difference of potential field distribution and adsorption ability of different structural nanotube arrays.

title: Fractal mechanics of hydrogen storage in the bundle of carbon nanotubes
Study on the preparation of carbon nanofiber washcoat by nickel foam and supported nickel catalyst
abstract: Carbon nanofiber is widely used in catalytic materials,hydrogen storage and nanoelectron device.Supported nickel catalyst together with nickel foam was used to synthesize carbon nanofiber washcoat by catalytic decomposition of ethylene or propylene in this paper.It was characterized by XRD,nitrogen physisorption and SEM analysis.The effect of catalyst type,carbon source and temperature on the yield and the morphology of carbon nanofibers were investigated.The results show that under the condition of grow temperature of 450℃ and ethylene flow rate of 30ml/min,the yield of carbon nanofibers using supported nickel catalyst is 3 to 6 times higher than nickel foam catalyst.The average diameter of carbon nanofibers from supported nickel catalyst is about 40 to 60 nanometers,which is smaller than the case of nickel foam catalyst.The yield and the average diameter of carbon nanofibers decrease with the decreasement of temperature.The lowerst temperature to grow carbon nanofibers on nickel foam catalyst is about 420℃ and the structure of nickel foam is not destroyed when the growth temperature is lower than 480℃,carbon nanofibers made by this way could potentially find applications as new type structured catalytic materials.

title: THE HYDROGEN STORAGE MECHANISM AND APPLICATION OF ONE DIMENSIONAL CARBON NANOMATERIALS
abstract: One dimensional carbon nanomaterials become a candidate with many advantages for hydrogen storage because of their high surface area and other special properties. A brief review of carbon nanofibers for hydrogen storage is given indicating that hydrogen storage capacity in carbon nanofibers is higher than in existing materials. An explanation of the mechanism of adsorptive storage in carbon nanofibers is introduced, in which physical and chemical absorption on surfaces and nanopores of the nanofibers may occur. It is pointed out that carbon nanofibers are the most feasible candidate for hydrogen storage technologies, but some problems such as how to increase the volume capacity for hydrogen storage, absorption and desorption hydrogen velocity and to decrease the operation pressure must be solved.

title: CO_2 Hydrogenation to Methanol over Cu-ZrO_2 Catalyst Promoted by Co-decorated CNTs
abstract: With the homemade Co-decorated multiwalled carbon nanotubes(y%Co/CNT) as promoter,a type of y%Co/CNT-promoted co-precipitated Cu-ZrO2 catalysts,CuiZrj-x%(y%Co/CNT),were developed.Over a Cu1Zr1-10%(4.3%Co/CNT) catalyst under reaction conditions of 5.0 MPa,513 K,V(H2)/V(CO2)/V(N2)=69/23/8 and GHSV=8 000 mL/(h·g),the observed turnover frequency(TOF) of CO2 hydrogenation reached 2.89×10-3 s-1.This value was 1.22 and 1.20 times that(2.36×10-3 s-1 and 2.40×10-3 s-1) of the CNT-free substrate Cu1Zr1 and the simple CNT-promoted counterpart Cu1Zr1-10%CNT,respectively,under the same reaction conditions.The selectivity of methanol in the CO2 hydrogenation products reached ~92%,with corresponding STY reaching 176 mg-CH3OH/(h·g-cat.).Characterization of the catalysts revealed that the hydrogen adsorption capacity of the Co-decorated CNT-promoted Cu1Zr1-based catalyst was considerably higher than that of the CNT-free substrate or the simple CNT-promoted counterpart.This would be favorable to generating a surface micro-environment with a high concentration of H-adspecies on the functioning catalyst,thus increasing the rate of surface CO2 hydrogenation reactions.

title: Effect of Pretreatment on Hydrogen Adsorption Storage of Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: Hydrogen adsorption of multi-walled carbon nanotubes(MWNTs) was investigated under moderate pressure(10 MPa) at 30 °C.The effects of pretreatment on the hydrogen adsorption of carbon nanotubes were discussed.MWNTs were synthesized by chemical vapor deposition(CVD) using iron nanoparticles embedded in mesoporous silica as catalyst.The microstructural characteristics of MWNTs before and after pretreatment were checked by transmission electron microcopy(TEM), scanning electron microscopy(SEM),X-ray diffraction(XRD),thermo-gravimetric analysis(TGA) and N_2 adsorption isotherms(BET).Both acid treatment and heat treatment play important roles in the hydrogen adsorption of carbon nanotubes.After removal of catalyst,the hydrogen storage capacity of MWNTs increased from 0.4% to 1.90%,and further up to 2.10% after heat treatment at 1 200 °C in N_2 atmosphere.

title: New One-dimension Materiales-Synthesis and Potential Application of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: The recent progress on single\|walled carbon nanotubes has been reviewed briefly in this paper. Main developments of synthetic technologies, including arc discharge, chemical vapor deposition, larser vaporization and solar approach, made in the past two years are described. The prospects for application in hydrogen storage material, nano\|scale electronic devices and carbon nanotube actuators aer outlined. Several key factors influencing the production and practical application of single\|walled carbon nanotubes have been discussed. The research direction of single\|walled acrbon nonotubes is also presented.

title: Research Progress on the Preparation and Application of Composite Materials Based on Grapheme
abstract: The preparation of both graphene and grapheme-based materials known as the nouveau riche inthe field of material science was reviewed and various applications were profiled in solar cell,super capaci-tor,hydrogen storage material,photocatalytic composite materials.The future development was prospected.

title: Adsorption of low concentration H_2S on impregnated activated carbon under anaerobic conditions
abstract: To investigate the enhancement of impregnation of sodium carbonate and relative humidity of the feed on the adsorption of low concentration H_2S on activated carbon under anaerobic conditions at ambient temperature,the experiments of dynamic adsorption of hydrogen sulfide on activated carbon and the impregnated one were carried out under different relative humidity.The effect of temperature on adsorption processes was also investigated. The results show that the adsorption equilibrium data were fitted well with the Freundlich Isotherm.Compared with the activated carbon,the BET surface area and the micropore volume of the impregnated ones were reduced slightly while the adsorption capacity of H_2S increased.This indicates that H2S reacts with the impregnant on the surface of activated carbon.When relative humidity is increased,the adsorption capacity is evidently enhanced on both of activated carbon and the impregnated one.The equilibrium adsorption capacity decreases and the breakthrough time reduce with the temperature increasing.

title: Template Synthesis,Activation and Energy Storage Application of Porous Carbon Materials
abstract: Porous carbon materials prepared by template synthesis has attracted much attention because of their promising applications in energy-related fields.The recent development of template synthesis was reviewed in details.And traditional activation method,which was applied to further tune pore structures of carbon materials prepared via template method was also introduced.Porous carbons used as hydrogen storage materials and electrode materials for supercapacitors were commented.

title: Computer Simulations of Hydrogen Storage in Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: The capability of hydrogen storage in zigzag single\|walled carbon nanotubes is investigated.Relations of diameter and length with the hydrogen reserves and the distribution of hydrogen storage in single\|walled carbon nanotubes are obtained.A new expression of hydrogen storage capability is presented.

title: Influence of CNTs content on the performance of AB_5 hydrogen storage alloys
abstract: AB5 type hydrogen storage alloys with different carbon nanotubes(CNTs) contents were synthesized by mechanical ball milling method.The effects of the CNTs contents on the microstructure and the electrochemical performance of the hydrogen storage alloys were studied.The results showed that the performance of hydrogen storage alloys was improved by adding CNTs.When the CNTs content was 15%,the specific capacity of the composite hydrogen storage alloys at the first discharge was 311 mAh/g,which was enhanced 21% as compared with that of the AB5 alloys,and the specific discharge capacity retained 280 mAh/g after 200 cycles.

title: THE PREPARATION OF SUPER-ACTIVATED CARBONS AND ITS PROPERTIES FOR HYDROGEN STORAGE
abstract: A series of super activated carbons were prepared from high sulfur petroleum cokes with orthogonal design L9(3 4). The adsorption of hydrogen was measured systematically on the super activated carbon with the surface area of 3?886?m 2/g covering a temperature range of 93?K～293?K at 20?K and a pressure range of 0?MPa～7?MPa. The results showed that the adsorption isotherms have the properties of Ⅰ style and its capacity for hydrogen storage is good. The hydrogen adsorption by weight was 1.9?W/%, 9.8?W/% in the condition of 293?K/5?MPa?93?K/6?MPa, and the isosteric heats was quite lower.

title: Activated carbon modification condition and its influence on the performance of the adsorption of hydrogen sulfide
abstract: The H2S adsorption breakthrough time and breakthrough capacity of industrial activated carbons which were untreated,modified by NaOH,Na2CO3,Fe(NO3)3,Cu(AC)2 impregnant respectively,and treated by oxidation sulfur bacteria biofilm were compared under the same condition.The results indicated that the activated carbon modified by NaOH was significantly better than any other modifier under the same condition.Compared with the modifier at different concentration of NaOH,the activated carbon modified by 20% NaOH had the best effect on the removal of hydrogen sulfide.The breakthrough time and the breakthrough capacity were 78.25 mg/g and 2000 min above respectively.After the oxidation sulfur bacteria biofilm was formed on the modified activated carbon,which had certain effect on the removal of hydrogen sulfide.The saturated activated carbon modified by NaOH can be regenerated by oxidation sulfur bacteria biofilm,and achieve 100% on the removal of hydrogen sulfide.The activated carbon treated by oxidation sulfur bacteria biofilm has a good effect on the removal of hydrogen sulfide.

title: Application of energy storage technology in small and medium wind power generation systems
abstract: The classification and application range of energy storage technologies are discussed,and the structure and energy storage effect of small and medium wind power generation systems are expounded,At the same time,the applications of the carbon nanotube super capacitor energy storage,hydrogen storage,hybrid energy storage about super capacitors and battery in small and medium wind power generation systems are analysised.

title: Experimental Research on Activated Carbon's Influence To The Hydrogen Storage Characteristics of THF Hydrates
abstract: The influence of activated carbon to the hydrogen storage characteristics of tetrahydrofuran(abbr.THF) hydrates using a high pressure stirring gas hydrate experimental apparatus in constant volume under the temperature of 1℃,pressure of 6.4MPa,7.4 MPa and 8.4 MPa,and the THF solution mole concentration of 5.0%.The results showed that when without adding activated carbon,the average induction time is 333min,and when adding activated carbon,the average induction time is 250min,so adding activated carbon can decrease the induction time at high pressure;when without adding activated carbon,the pressure drop are 0.028 MPa,0.035 MPa,0.040 MPa respectively,and when adding activated carbon,the pressure drop are 0.030 MPa,0.040 MPa,0.090 MPa respectively,so adding activated carbon can improve the pressure drop,and the higher the pressure,the larger the pressure drop;when without adding activated carbon,the hydrogen storage capacity by weight are 0.0026%,0.0033%,0.0031% respectively,and when adding activated carbon,the hydrogen storage capacity by weight are 0.0041%,0.0048%,0.0082% respectively,so adding activated carbon can improve the hydrogen storage capacity by weight,and the higher the pressure,the larger the hydrogen storage capacity by weight.

title: DETERMINATION OF ISOSTERIC HEAT OF ADSORPTION OF HYDROGEN ON CARBON-BASED ADSORBENTS WITH NONLOCAL DENSITY FUNCTIONAL THEORY APPROACH
venue: Journal of Chemical Industry and Engineering
abstract: To evaluate the hydrogen adsorption performance of the typical carbon based adsorbents from the aspect of adsorption heat, nonlocal density functional theory(NDFT),Carnahan-Starling, MBWR equations of state and the mean-field theory are used to determine the bulk density and density profiles of hydrogen molecules within the adsorption space.The adsorption density is obtained from the weighted average of the density profile calculated with NDFT in the width (or radial) direction of adsorption space. The maximum physical adsorption capacities of hydrogen molecules in the close-packing state are used to calculate the isosteric heat of adsorption. The adsorption isotherms at 77-297 K with a step of 10 K and 1-10 MPa with a step of 1 kPa are first determined,then,the isosteric heat of adsorption on three typical carbon based adsorbents are ascertained by the adsorbed phase volume and the bulk gas volume in thermodynamic equilibrium during the adsorption process.From the comparisons among the results from the NDFT calculation and experimental data,not only the isotherms of hydrogen adsorption on carbon nanotubes have similar figure to those of activated carbon,but also the values of isosteric heat of adsorption on these adsorbents are within the same range.Finally,the measure that the accurate hydrogen adsorption experiments on pure carbon nanotubes should be carried out to verify their physical adsorption performance,and the effective measures for the management of adsorption heat should also be emphasized while considering the cryogenic adsorption of hydrogen in carbon nanotubes.

title: Recent progress of N-doped porous carbon materials
abstract: Functionalization,such as nitrogen atom doping,will enhance intrinsic and/or add new features to porous carbons,thus making the best of their potential applications.Recently,a series of methodologies have been developed to prepare nitrogen-doped porous carbons with special structures and properties.Based on the progress made in recent years concerning N-doped porous carbons,the synthesis strategies for N-doped porous carbon,including liquid template,chemical vapor deposition,post treatment with ammonia,chemical activation and hydrothermal process,are introduced.The characteristics and limitations of various methods are also commented.In addition to the summary of the present applications in catalysis,gas adsorption/separation,hydrogen storage and removal of pollutant gases of these novel carbon materials,the development directions of large-scale preparation of N-doped porous carbons for industrial applications are presented.

title: Study on Preparation of Activated Carbons from Walnut Shells and Odor Gas Adsorption
abstract: The paper studied the process conditions of preparing activated carbon from walnut shells using the method of ZnCl2 activation,and the sulfide capacity and penetration behavior of the adsorption of hydrogen sulfide before and after the modification process.The results showed that when the mass fraction of ZnCl2 is 60%,the carbonization temperature is 300 ℃ and the time is 80 min,the activation temperature is 500 ℃ and the time is 60 min,the activated carbon takes on the highest sulfur capacity and a long breakthrough time.Characterization of its performance showed that the measured iodine adsorption value can reach to 880 mg/g,much better than commercially available activated carbon adsorption.The desulfurization performance of activated carbons modified by 1% KIO3 has improved significantly.

title: Press hydrogen storage of multi-walled carbon nanotubes
venue: Journal of Anhui University of Technology
abstract: Multi-wall nanotube was prepared with floating catalyst method. It was treated with heating, mixed acid or doped Li. They were stored hydrogen under p (H2)=12, 9 MPa at room temperature. Different treating methods affected hydrogen storage in multi-walled carbon nanotubes. The hydrogen storage capacity of carbon nanotube doped Li was the biggest.

title: Mechanical Analysis and Optimal Control of Hydrogen Storage Vessels with Carbon Fiber Filament Wound Aluminum Liner
abstract: Basing on the theory of classical laminated plates and the theory of the grid,the model of filament wound metal-lined pressure vessels were simplified,and the orthotropic assumption was proposed,including the viewpoint that the material stays at linear elasticity and the fiber can withstand the stress;Having the coupling of tension stress and shear stress of enhancement layers in composite pressure vessel ignored to get stress distribution of the model with internal or external pressure.Fiber-preload control was put forward to optimize the stress distribution.The experimental model proves the rationality of both theoretical derivation and control method.

title: Development of Research on Carbon and Organic Hydrogen Storage Material
abstract: Due to the serious problems caused by energy crisis and environmental pollution,much attention are focused on developing clean renewable energy.Hydrogen,for its renewable and pollution-free characteristics,has become the most potential energy carrier.Hydrogen storage is one of the most challenging technologies for hydrogen application.In this article,two kinds of hydrogen storage materials are introduced:carbon hydrogen storage material and organic hydrogen storage material.Among the carbon hydrogen storage material,activated carbon,carbon fiber,and carbon nanotuber are introduced;In the organic hydrogen storage material,organic liquid and metal organic are introduced.In the meantime,new development of carbon and organic hydrogen storage material is reviewed.The article proposes a possible development trend in this research field,puts forward a key of developing a novel porous material and probing into a novel metal organic hydrogen storage material is the development of metal organic porous material.

title: The Effect of Microlitic Carbon in Mg-based Composite Hydrogen-stored Materials
venue: Journal of Shandong University of Science and Technology
abstract: In order to improve the hydrogen-release dynamic performance of metal magnesium,the microlitic carbon prepared from anthracite by demineralization and carbonization was used to add into the magnesium powders to produce the magnesium-carbon composed hydrogen-stored materials with high performance by reactive ball milling method under hydrogen atmosphere.The structure of microlitic carbon was characterized by the X-ray diffraction and infrared spectrum,and that of the hydrogen-stored material was tested by the transmission electron microscope,X-ray energy spectrum,and powder X-ray diffraction.The performance of hydrogen-storage for materials was investigated by differential scanning calorimetry and p-c-T test.The results show that the microlitic carbon is of similar structure to graphite,the carbon acts as milling aid for magnesium powder during ball milling,and the synergistic effect for hydrogenation and dehydrogenation occurs between magnesium and microlitic carbon.With the addition of 40% of microlitic carbon,the magnesium particles are milled to 30～50 nm in 2 h and the initial dehydrogenation temperature of the resulted hydrogen-stored material decreases to 227.4 ℃ as well as the hydrogen-stored density is up to 6.7%.

title: The Single-Wall Carbon Nanotube and Its Application
abstract: The unique structure of single-wall carbon nanotube makes it have a unique electricity mature, absorption and mechanics properties. The application and research of single-wall carbon nanotube in the fields as electronics, hydrogen storage and compound materials are comprehensively expounded after a discussion of the unique structure, characteristics and methods of preparing and making it.

title: Determination of impurity oxygen and nitrogen in hydrogen storage alloy based on mixed rare earth metals
abstract: The determination of impurity oxygen and nitrogen in hydrogen-storage alloy based on mixed rare earth metals was studied.While being heated to high temperature,the rare earth metals can easily volatilize,which will have bad effect on the determination.So suitable conditions were chosen for the determination including appropriate heating temperature,appropriate graphite bath,nickel as supplementary agent for melting and high temperature crucible with upper-lower seat being used.Low and stable blank values of the bath material and supplementary agent were supposed.The proposed method has been applied to the determination of impurity oxygen and nitrogen in hydrogen-storage alloy based on mixed rare earth metals.The samples contain oxygen of 0.43% and nitrogen of 0.018%,the analysis precisions are 4.3% for oxygen and 5.9% for nitrogen;the recoveries are in the range of 93%～104% for oxygen and 92%～110% for nitrogen.

title: Theoretical study of hydrogen adsorption in single-walled carbon nanotubes by first principles molecular dynamics method
venue: Journal of Atomic and Molecular Physics
abstract: Adsorption of hydrogen molecules in finite chiral single-walled carbon nanotubes(SWCNTs) was presented using the first-principles plane-wave pseudopotential molecular dynamics simulations method.The hydrogen storages of different diameter nanotubes were studied.The simulation results of hydrogen storage in SWCNTs show that:(1) When the physisorption happens,the H_2 can adsorb in both the cavity of tube and the crevice between tubes.The hydrogen adsorption energy of SWCNTs inner is all higher than that outside of the tube,but the intact H_2 molecules can t go through the tube wall and enter tube inner.(2) When the chemisorption happens,the hydrogen adsorption first appears at the edge of SWCNTs.C atoms bonded with H atoms result in the structural deformation in parts of tube wall and tension of SWCNTs would aggrandize with the increment of the C-H bonds,so the system is unsteady.(3) Along with the increment of the diameter,the difference of hydrogen adsorption capability between the inside and outside of each SWCNT drops off.

title: Advance in Synthesis and Application of Mesoporous Carbon
abstract: The synthesis method and application of the mesoporous carbon were reviewed,and the template synthesis methods,including inorganic template method,mesoporous molecular sieves method and organic template method,were introduced in detail. It is suggested that organic template synthesis method is prospective. Mesoporous carbon has many applications,as a catalyst carrier,it should be given adequate attention,and the mesoporous carbon used as hydrogen-storage material and energy-storage material should be focused on in future.

title: The influence of chemical potential on computer simulation of hydrogen storage in single-walled carbon nanotubes
abstract: Widom test particle method is perfected firstly for calculating chemical potential.And then,the computing method of pressure for fluid systems with periodic boundary conditions is adopted to investigate the relation between chemical potential and bulk pressure in an open system.The chemical potential as a function of the bulk pressure is presented,and its correctness is proved.Based on these,the influence of chemical potential on computer simulation of hydrogen storage in single-walled carbon nanotubes(SWCNTs) is analyzed in detail by the grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations.Our computational results show that the influence of chemical potential with little difference on computer simulation of hydrogen storage in SWCNTs is very remarkable.

title: THEORETICAL STUDY ON THE EXCESS ADSORPTION OF HYDROGEN UNDER SUPERCRITICAL STATE IN MICROPORES OF CARBONACEOUS ADSORBENTS
abstract: The development of the supercritical adsorption theory plays a key role in evaluating the adsorptive performance of the carbon adsorbents in hydrogen storage.A new Ono-Kondo equation,based on the lattice theory,is developed to describe the supercritical fluid adsorption inside the slit-shaped micropores of adsorbents.The analytical solution to the equation is applied to predict the hydrogen adsorption at supercritical high-pressure inside the pores of the adsorbents.On the basis of the hydrogen adsorption data on activated carbon AX-21,the analytical solution is further modified to evaluate the applicable range of the theory.The accuracy of the defined Ono-Kondo equation is verified by comparing the predicted results with other hydrogen adsorption data and with those from the GCMC molecular simulation on AX-21 activated carbon over the temperature range 77～298 K and for pressure up to 30 MPa.The good agreement between the predicted results and the experimental data confirms the reasonability of the fixed values for the equation.

title: Analysis of Instability of Field Electron Emission from Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: Multiwalled carbon nanotubes were synthesized by plasma-enhanced hot filament chemical vapor deposition and their characteristics of field electron emission were measured.It is found that the characteristics are changed.After they were characterized by energy dispersive X-ray,the result indicates that oxygen is adsorbed on them.The adsorption of oxygen results in the change of work function of carbon nanotube so that the characteristics become instable.Simultaneously,the possible effects of the adsorption of hydrogen on their characteristics of field electron emission were analyzed as well.So,it is believed that this work is significance for applications of carbon nanotubes in the field of microelectronics.

title: Application of Nano-material in Automobile Industry
venue: Journal of Chongqing Institute of Technology
abstract: This paper deals with the research and application of nano-technology in automobile coating, gasoline, lubricant, off-gas clarifier, nano-plastic and nano-structured carbon materials with high hydrogen storage.

title: Monte carlo simulations of hydrogen physisorption on single-layer graphene
venue: Yunnan Daxue xuebao. Shehui kexue ban
abstract: The physisorption behavior of hydrogen molecules adsorbed on single-layer graphene is simulated using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo(GCMC)approach.The simulations are carried out at temperature 77 — 473K and under the pressure in the range of 0.1 —10MPa.The results show that under the conditions of low-temperature and high-pressure the hydrogen storage on single-layer graphene is more effective.At 10MPa pressure,isosteric heat with increasing temperature first decreases then increases.The lowest isosteric heat is found at 291K.

title: Synthesis of Carbon Nanotubes with Open Ends
abstract: The method of chemical vapor deposition (CVD) has been applied in the synthesis of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with alcohol as carbon source. By means of TEM and Raman spectrum methods, the morphology and structure of carbon nanotubes have been investigated, and the relationship between these CNTs and the experimental parameters such as catalysts and reaction conditions has been discussed. It is indicated that compared with the CNTs synthesized in other methods, CNTs synthesized here have bigger inside diameter, fewer defects and open ends when the experimental parameters are controlled stably. CNTs of these structures have better performances in hydrogen-storage and so on, and have greater potential applications.

title: PURIFICATION AND HYDROGEN ADSORPTION OF SINGLE-WALLED CARBON NANOTUBES
abstract: The purification of single-walled carbon nanotubes(SWNTs)synthesized by a hydrogen arc-discharge method was investigated.After treated by using a HNO3 and H2O2 reflux method,the impurities of amorphous carbon,carbon nanoparticles and metal catalysts that initially co-existed with the as-prepared SWNTs were removed effectively.Based on the results of electron microscopy observations and thermo-gravimetric analysis,the purity of the purified sample was estimated to be above 95% at a yield of about 35%.The effect of the H2O2 reflux treatment on the pore structure of the purified SWNTs was studied.It is shown that the pore distribution and specific surface area of the SWNTs can be significantly influenced by the purification process.The hydrogen adsorption property of the SWNTs was investigated by using a volumetric testing method.The hydrogen storage capacity of the purified SWNTs was 1.65%,evidently higher than that(0.56%)of the as-prepared SWNTs sample.

title: Development of carbon materials for fuel cell
abstract: As key materials for fuel cell, carbon materials, which have unique physical and chemical properties and various forms, are widely applied in new type battery industry. Development and application of carbon materials, especially in some components of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC), such as the electrode substrate, bipolar plate, catalyst layer support and hydrogen storage materials, were reviewed. The manufacture process and properties of electrode substrate and bipolar are also involved. The effect of particle size and morphology of supported carbon on catalyst activity is investigated, and the uptake development of hydrogen storage materials in fuel cell is also evaluated.

title: Preparation and research status of graphene
abstract: Preparation methods of graphene are introduced,which include mechanical exfoliation,reduction graphite oxide,annealing of SiC and chemical vapor deposition methods,etc.The characteristics as well as problems of various preparation methods are analyzed.Besides,graphene used for nanoelectronic devices,the computer chip to replace the silicon,to create the fastest carbon transistors,reduce noise and in the fields of potential hydrogen storage materials are discussed,the effects of the structure of graphene on property are described and its future development is prospected.

title: Experimental and Theoretical Progress of Hydrogen Storage in Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: The development of investigation for materials of hydrogen storage is briefly reviewed,mainly about the presently experimental advancement of carbone nanotubes(CNTs).In the aspect of theoretical study,a theory of decomposition and condensation mechanism(DCM) is proposed for the hydrogen storage of the single\|walled carbone nanotubes(SWNT).\;

title: The application of molecular simulation on carbon nanotube research
abstract: This article refers to the recent developments of computer molecular modeling technique applied in the research of carbon nanotubes. The applications include the study of nanotube's mechanic properties, electromagnetic properties,reactivity properties, hydrogen storage capability and the research of the polymer/carbon-nanotubes composites.

title: Research Progress in Application of Carbon Nanotubes in the Field of Energy
abstract: Carbon nanotubes as a new type of carbon materials have complete molecular structure. On the structure, it has the special shape of hollow tubes configuration, good electrical conductivity, high specific surface area, good chemical stability, the space for electrolyte ion migration and the network structure of nanometer scale through winding and interaction. As electrode materials, it can well improve the power characteristics, stability and other aspects of capacitors and fuel cells. Special hollow structure and high specific surface area make it become a hydrogen storage material with great application potential. In this paper, application and research progress of carbon nanotubes in hydrogen storage materials, super capacitors and fuel cells were introduced.

title: Progress of doped graphene nanocomposites
abstract: Graphene has unique structure and excellent performance,and its preparation methods are presented.The emphasis is focused on the major doping methods of graphene nanocomposites,such as element doping methods,including non-metallic elements and metallic elements doping methods,compounds doping methods and carbon materials doping methods.These nanocomposite materials are widely used,especially in the supercapacitor,sensor,hydrogen storage,and biomedical areas.Some problems about the processing of grapheme are presented,such as easily getting folded,instability of dispersion and so on.The future trend of application is discussed,for example magnetism and optical property.

title: Instability Analysis and Development of High Pressure Hydrogen Storage Vessels
abstract: Making use of ANSYS software,the instability of each order's modality for the 4mm-thick liner of high-pressure hydrogen storage container which made of carbon fiber composite material was implemented.Considering the prestress and safety margin,the 4mm-thick liner was selected. The fatigue test in rapid hydrogen-charging and discharging environment was conducted for a 70 MPa high-pressure hydrogen storage vessel,including other tests like pressure test,impact resistance test and burst test. The test results prove the vessel safety.

title: Autofrettage Analysis and Prediction of Burst Pressure of Carbon Fiber-winding Hydrogen Storage Vessels by FEM
abstract: The finite element model embedded isotropy metal and anisotropy composite material is established according to the structure characteristics of the high pressure hydrogen storage vessel with metal liner and carbon fiber-winding layers.Static elasto-plastic stress and deformation simulations are carried out under various pressure loads,with considering the effect of autofrettage and working conditions and also referring DOT CFFC standard.Based on the progressive failure theory,Tsai-Wu failure criteria was employed to determine the failure properties of composite vessels,according to which the stiffness of relevant elements is modified.The birth-to-death element technique in the finite element analysis is used to describe the mechanical properties of carbon fiber composite elements.The burst pressure of the vessel predicted in terms of the rapid increasing of the number of failure elements with increasing internal pressure is in good agreement with the experimental results,which proved the acceracy of the proposed approach.

title: Synthesis of Three-dimensional Graphene Architectures and Their Applications in Energy and Environmental Fields
abstract: Graphene has attracted great attention and interest from global scientists. The fabrication methods and applications of three-dimensional graphene are under initial stage, thus, this review aims to describe the different synthetic processes for preparation three-dimensional graphene architectures and their merits and demerits; Moreover, the different fields of application such as adsorption, capacitive deionization, microbial fuel cells, supercapacitor and hydrogen storage are also reviewed; Finally, suggestions for further research are presented in the end of the paper.

title: THE STUDY ON PREPARATION AND CHARACTERISTICS OF COMPOSITE HYDROGEN STORAGE MATERIALS OF MAGNESIUM BASED ALLOYS WITH CARBON NANOFIBERS(I)—PREPARATION OF Mg_2Ni-CNFs COMPOSITE HYDROGEN STORAGE MATERIAL BY THERMAL DIFFUSION METHOD WITH ELECTROLESS
abstract: As magnesium can be alloyed with other metals easily, a kind of composite hydrogen storage material of Mg-Ni alloy with carbon nanofibers(CNFs) is prepared by thermal diffusion with electroless nickel plated carbon nanofibers(Ni-CNFs) as precursor. The electrochemical performance of this composite hydrogen storage material is tested, while its mechanism of hydrogen storage is proposed.$$$$

title: Effect of Milling Time on the Electrochemical Properties of AB_5/10 wt.% CNTs Composite Hydrogen Storage Alloys
abstract: Mm(NiCoMnAl)5/10wt.% CNT composite hydrogen storage alloys are prepared by ball milling Mm(NiCoMnAl)5 with a small amount of CNTs as addition under an atmosphere of high purity argon.Structures and electrochemical properties of the composite alloys are investigated systematically by X-ray diffraction,scanning electron microscope and electrochemical experiments.The results indicate that the composite alloys possess a structure of CaCu5 on whose surface a plenty of CNTs are bonded.The content of CNTs in composite alloys decreases with increasing milling time.The electrochemical studies show that maximum discharge capacity,the capacity retention after 60 cycles and high rate discharge-ability of the composite alloys increase firstly and then decrease with increasing milling time.The alloy milled for 5 h exhibits the best maximum discharge capacity(291.9 mAh/g).And the alloy milled for 3 h is the best capacity retention after 60 charge-discharge cycles(91.2%) and high rate dischargeability.

title: The Progress of Inorganic Materials for Hydrogen Storage
abstract: Hydrogen energy becomes green energy for the 21st century to solve the crisis of fossil energy in the future and reduce the pollution for fossil consumption.Hydrogen storage and transportation are critical problems for realizing application of hydrogen energy.This paper simply introduces general feature of high-pressure hydrogen gas storage,liquid hydrogen storage and materials-mediated hydrogen storage systems.We mainly review the development of inorganic materials for hydrogen storage,such as metal,metal oxides,carbon-based materials,chemical hydrides,M-N-H system and M-C-H system.Up to now,the results of hydrogen storage investigation still do not meet the target of International Energy Agency at present.Therefore preparation about inorganic composite materials and the mechanism of thermodynamic and kinetics for hydrogen storage in the materials need to be studied further.

title: Research progress of hydrogen storage in carbon nanotubes
abstract: The results of experiments of hydrogen storage in carbon nanotubes as well as theoretical calculations were reviewed,and the latest development of hydrogen storage in nanotubes was introduced.Different methods were compared and analyzed,and the feasibility of hydrogen in carbon nanotubes was discussed.The prospective application of carbon nanotubes as excellent adsorbents was presented.

title: Status quo and Progress in Application Research of Carbon Nanotube
abstract: The status quo and recent progress in application research of carbon nanotube is reviewed, including the field-emission,molecule electronic device, composite materials, super capacitor,hydrogen storage materials, Li-ion rechargeable battery electrode materials, catalyst materials, and so on. In the meantime, the advances and existing problems of application are evaluated; the application prospect of carbon nanotube is also forecasted.

title: Texture and Hydrogen Adsorption of Activated Carbons Based on Hemp Stems
abstract: Hemp stems were used as raw materials and high-surface-area activated carbons were prepared through chemical activation with KOH as active agent in different activation times. The sample was treated with HNO3 to study the effect of surface modification on adsorption capacity. The properties of the resulting samples were characterized by N2 adsorption-desorption techniques and FTIR. Hydrogen storage capacities at 77 K and 100 kPa were also determined. All samples obtain high surface areas(2 435.93~3 240.95 m2·g-1) and total pore volumes(1.3~1.98 cm3·g-1). Both of the surface area and total pore volumes increase with increasing activation time. As the activation time increase more than 3.5 h, both of the surface area and total pore volumes descend, which is due to the structure collapse. Pore size distributions were nearly similar and show multimodal dominated by micropores smaller than 2 nm with a small amount of meso/macropores. The maximum hydrogen uptake measured for the sample activated at 800 ℃ for 3.5 h reached 3.28wt%(in gravimetric). Hydrogen adsorption is controlled mainly by textural properties such as surface area and pore volume. At 77 K, not only micropores smaller than 2 nm but also mesopores contribute to the hydrogen adsorption. Treatment with HNO3 lowered surface areas, total pore volumes and hydrogen adsorption capacities.

title: Theoretical study on hydrogen storage in single-walled boron nitride nanotubes
abstract: The hydrogen storage in single-walled boron nitride nanotubes(SWBNNT) is simulated by Monte Carlo method on the condition of moderate pressure at normal temperature.The influences of tube diameter,tube length,tube chirality and pressure on hydrogen physisorption in SWBNNT are investigated emphatically.Compared with the hydrogen physisorption in single-walled carbon nanotubes,the hydrogen storage capability of SWBNNT is greater than the other.Our computational results show that the hydrogen storage capacity(mass percent) of SWBNNT at normal temperature and moderate pressure can reach the commercial standard,which is presented by the U.S.Department of Energy.

title: Preparation of Isolated Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes with High Hydrogen Storage Capacity
abstract: Isolated single-walled carbon nanotubes with high proportion of opening tips were synthesized by using alcohol as carbon source. The mechanism of cutting action of oxygen was proposed to explain its growth. Compared with carbon nanotubes synthesized with benzene as carbon source,their specific surface area was heightened by approximately 2.2 times (from 200.5 to 648 m2/g) and the hydrogen storage capacity was increased by approximately 6.5 times (from 0.95 to 7.17%,ω) which had exceeded DOE energy standard of vehicular hydrogen storage.

title: Effect of heat treatment on hydrogen adsorption storage of multi-walled carbon nanotubes
venue: Journal of Hefei University of Technology
abstract: Adsorption isotherms of hydrogen on multi-walled carbon nanotubes(MWNT) were obtained using the volumetric method under moderate pressure(10 MPa) at room temperature.The effect of heat treatment on the microstructure and hydrogen adsorption of carbon nanotubes was discussed.The MWNTs were characterized by transmission electron microcopy(TEM),Raman spectroscopy,and N2 adsorption isotherms(BET).It was found that the crystal parameters were increased after heat treatment.The hydrogen storage capacity of carbon nanotubes was found to increase from 1.90 % to 2.17 % after the heat treatment.

title: Properties of metal hydride's adsorption and feasibility of activated carbon in storing hydrogen
venue: Journal of North China Electric Power University
abstract: In order to utilize hydrogen energy the difficulties from hydrogen's transportation and storage should be solved. This paper established a heat transfer and mass transfer model composed of three concentric cylinders. The simulation and research manifest that the front of hydrogen adsorption reaction moves faster at the initial period than other periods. The higher the hydrogen pressure level while hydrides metal absorbs hydrogen, the faster the reaction is. Thermal conductivity in hydrides metal has a great effect on the rate of hydriding and dehydriding reaction. Therefore, the adsorption reaction of thinner layer should be used to store hydrogen, In the view of reducing the weight and raising the performance, activated carbon is more suitable for vehicles' hydrogen storage than metal hydrides because of its gentle adsorption, light weight and low cost

title: Fitting Function of Potential Energy of H_2 out of Sidewall in the H_2 Storage of Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: The potential energy curve between H_2 and carbon nanotubes is an important content in the field of hydrogen storage simulation and building the formula about the potential energy curve has value in the theoretical research and practical application.In this paper,potential energy model between H_2 and carbon atom was built with Lennard-Jones potential energy by using molecular dynamics,and the potential energy curve between hydrogen molecules and carbon nanotube was computed.We acquired optimal parameters through fitting the curve of H_2 potential energy outside the tube,and got the formula of H_2 potential energy outside the tube,thus found the place of maximum storing hydrogen capacity outside SWNT,which provided the theoretical reference for the study of the SWNTs.

title: Pressure influence on hydrogen adsorption in carbon nanomaterials
venue: Journal of Tsinghua University(Science and Technology)
abstract: Fuel cell vehicles are truly green since they do not pollute the environment. However, there is no safe and efficient hydrogen storage technology for fuel cell vehicles. This paper studies the hydrogen storage capacity of carbon nanotubes and carbon nanofibers at ambient temperature. Hydrogen adsorption in prepared carbon nanomaterials is measured by the volume method at a constant temperature of 25 ℃ for pressure from 1 to 14 MPa. The carbon nanomaterials have the greatest hydrogen adsorption capacity at 25 ℃ when the equilibrium pressure is between 9～10 MPa. The maximum hydrogen adsorption capacity in the pretreated carbon nanotubes is about 3.1%. The physical mechanism is described in this paper.

title: Influence of carbon nanotubes addition on the performance of LaNi_5 hydrogen storage materials
abstract: The preparation of the composite materials of carbon nanotubes(CNTs) and LaNi5 hydrogen storage alloys was researched by mechanical methods, and the relationship of the electrochemical hydrogen storage properties of new composite materials and the content of the CNTs was studied. The results show that the properties of LaNi5 hydrogen storage alloys is improved by adulterating CNTs, and when the CNTs content is 15%, the discharge capacity of the composite materials has achieved 311 mAh/g which is enhanced 21% compared to the LaNi5 alloys, and after 200 discharge cycles the discharge capacity is still as high as 280 mAh/g. The composite materials display good synergism and circulates performance。

title: Comments on hydrogen storage function of carbon material
Hydrogen storage in new nanostructured carbon materials
abstract: Hydrogen is a clean and renewable energy carrier. Because conventional materials and technologies for hydrogen storage cannot meet the needs of fuelcellpowered automobiles, how to store hydrogen more efficiently to reach the DOE target has become one of the most urgent and difficult problems to be solved in hydrogen applications. In recent years, storing hydrogen with various nanostructured carbon materials has attracted worldwide interest. However, there has been a great deal of controversy and divergent viewpoints. In this paper, hydrogen storage in various nanostructured carbon materials including singlewall nanotubes, multiwall nanotubes, graphite nanofibers and carbon nanofibers was reviewed. Some questions to be answered were pointed out, which include the standardization of the measuring method for hydrogen storage, characteristics of nanostructured carbon materials with high hydrogen storage capacity, the adsorption mechanism of hydrogen, etc.

title: Recent Researches and Developments on BN Nanotubes
abstract: The rencent progress on BN nanotubes is reviewed. Structure features and synthetic technology, (especially) chemical-synthesis routes and the corresponding growth mechanism, are summarized. BN nanotubes have a uniform electronic band gap of 5.5 eV, which is independent of tube diameter, chirality, or the number of tube walls. This property is different from that of carbon nanotubes. BN nanotubes can be used to fabricate some BN nanocomposites owing to their high chemical stability and thermal resistibility. BN nanotubes are promoted as a promising hydrogen storage material because of their highly porous structure and light mass density.
